reviewNote: Drafted by Claude from the chart for faculty review. Not validated teaching content.
summary: Symptomatic carotid stenosis 3 weeks after TIA, arriving with BP 192/104 because he stopped amlodipine 10 days ago (home log in the 170s, portal message never answered), on intentional DAPT.

asa.rationale: Symptomatic carotid disease, CAD with prior DES, diabetes, uncontrolled hypertension.

decision.recommendation: control BP first, then proceed today if possible
decision.rationale: Symptomatic carotid disease is time sensitive (ideally within 2 weeks of TIA), so avoid cancelling for weeks. Treat BP now toward under 180/110 with a reliable agent and confirm no end organ symptoms; proceed when controlled.

redFlags.evidence: 188/102 and 192/104; amlodipine stopped about 10/14 for edema; home BP 162 to 178 systolic; portal message 10/23 with no provider reply.
redFlags.implication: Labile intraop BP, myocardial ischemia, postoperative hyperperfusion syndrome and hematoma.
redFlags.action: Treat before induction (IV labetalol or a calcium channel blocker infusion), arterial line pre induction, tight postop SBP 100 to 140.

redFlags.evidence: TIA 10/06; CTA and duplex; small R A1 (weaker collateral).
redFlags.implication: Perfusion depends on BP during clamping.
redFlags.action: Arterial line, EEG, keep MAP at or above baseline during clamp, shunt ready, heparin 100 units/kg before clamp.

redFlags.finding: Continuing aspirin and clopidogrel by design
redFlags.evidence: Neurology and vascular: do not hold.
redFlags.action: Meticulous hemostasis, smooth emergence without coughing or hypertension, airway plan for hematoma.

planItems.item: Vasoactive infusions ready in both directions (phenylephrine and nicardipine or clevidipine)
Cefazolin 2 g within 60 min of incision
Smooth emergence, neuro exam in the OR
Step down or ICU, SBP 100 to 140
